questions.stem: What two forces are in equilibrium during a star's main sequence phase?

options.text: Gravitational collapse inward and radiation pressure outward

questions.explanation: During the main sequence phase, a star is in hydrostatic equilibrium. The inward pull of gravity is balanced by the outward radiation pressure produced by nuclear fusion in the core. This balance keeps the star stable for most of its lifetime.

questions.stem: What is the first stage in the formation of a star?

options.text: A white dwarf begins to accumulate mass
A cloud of gas and dust (nebula) begins to collapse under gravity
A red giant sheds its outer layers

questions.explanation: Star formation begins when a cloud of gas and dust, known as a nebula, starts to collapse under its own gravitational attraction. As the material contracts, it heats up, eventually forming a protostar.
